preliminary

/prih-LIM-uh-nair-ee/ — stress LIM: 'pre-LIM-inary' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Preliminary is coming before and preparing for the main, more important thing.

Preliminary sketches of the mural must be approved before any paint touches the wall.

Example

Before the orchestra's grand concert, the musicians held a short preliminary session that afternoon to test the hall's acoustics and mark the trickiest passages. Only after that came the real performance that evening.

Preliminary work comes before and prepares for the main event. Something merely 'early' just happens near the start; something preliminary exists specifically to lead up to what matters most.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

introductory: Introductory describes what opens a subject for an audience — an introductory chapter or course welcomes newcomers in. Preliminary points forward instead: a preliminary step exists specifically to prepare the ground for the main, more important thing that follows it.

preparatory: Preparatory means done to get someone or something ready, and it is preliminary's closest neighbor. The difference is emphasis: preparatory stresses the getting-ready work itself, while preliminary stresses sequence — it names the stage that comes just before the main event.

initial: Initial simply means occurring at the very start — the initial letter of a name, an initial payment. It says nothing about purpose. A preliminary step is more than merely first: it comes before the main thing precisely in order to prepare for it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

final: coming at the end; last

concluding: bringing something to a close

Where it sits · how much later steps depend on it

early → preliminary → foundational

early vs. preliminary: Early is weaker than preliminary — early just means near the start, while preliminary means the step exists specifically to prepare for the main event.

foundational vs. preliminary: Foundational is stronger than preliminary — a preliminary step leads up to the main thing, but a foundational one is what everything afterward is built upon.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pre-: before (Latin)

root — limin-: threshold, doorway (Latin)

suffix — -ary: relating to (Latin)

Put it together: Latin limen means 'threshold' — the strip at the bottom of a doorway. Something preliminary happens 'before the threshold': it stands just outside the door of the main event, preparing you to step through.

Use the root in a new word: eliminate: The first round of the spelling bee will eliminate half of the contestants.

Word Building

Word Choice

Common in sports, science, and law: preliminary rounds, preliminary results, preliminary hearings — all steps before the main event.
